title: db_integration_test.zig TC-DB-01-01/02 use unqualified `schema_migrations` reference, which silently resolves to a stray legacy tenant_default.schema_migrations shadow table under the tenant_default,public search_path instead of public.schema_migrations
notes:
Discovered by BACKEND-DEV while validating the ISS-0107 (GitHub #366) fix. The db_test container (port 5434) carried a stray, permanently-empty legacy tenant_default.schema_migrations shadow table (a pre-ISS-0091 artifact left over from before migration tracking was consolidated onto public.schema_migrations per src/design/iss504_migration_tracking.md). db_integration_test.zig's TC-DB-01-01 (line 65) and TC-DB-01-02 (lines 107/127) issue an unqualified `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schema_migrations` query. Under the tenant_default,public search_path used by TestHarness, this unqualified reference silently resolves to the stray tenant_default shadow copy (which is always empty) instead of public.schema_migrations (which holds 100+ real rows), causing the test to fail with a misleading 'count is 0' symptom that looks like a migration/locking bug but is actually a name-resolution defect combined with contaminated long-lived container state. This caused TC-DB-01-01/02 to fail via a DIFFERENT mechanism than ISS-0106 (ISS-503 concurrency) or ISS-0107 (advisory-lock/lock_timeout interaction) in 2 of BACKEND-DEV's 3 ISS-0107 validation runs, before being identified and worked around (DROP TABLE tenant_default.schema_migrations) to isolate the other two mechanisms for clean measurement.

This matches the pre-existing anti-pattern already catalogued in docs/anti-patterns.md ('Writing unqualified SQL in an integration test that exercises a GBL-prefixed (public-only) migration's effect, while the test connection's search_path is tenant_default,public' -- GitHub #338 / ISS-0089) but is a distinct occurrence in a different test file.
root_cause: tests/integration/db_integration_test.zig's TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02 use an unqualified `schema_migrations` table reference instead of explicitly schema-qualifying it as `public.schema_migrations`. Combined with a long-lived db_test container that still carries a stray, empty tenant_default.schema_migrations shadow table (leftover from before migration tracking was consolidated onto the public schema), the unqualified reference resolves to the wrong (always-empty) copy under the tenant_default,public search_path.
candidate_resolution: (a) Schema-qualify the reference in TC-DB-01-01/02 as `public.schema_migrations`, matching the pattern already established elsewhere in this file and prescribed by the existing anti-patterns.md entry for GBL-scoped migration tests. (b) Separately, consider whether tenant_default.schema_migrations should be dropped from any long-lived shared db_test container as one-time cleanup, and/or whether tools/clean_test_db.py or a schema-provisioning path should be audited to ensure it is never recreated for new tenant schemas going forward.
files_to_change_note: Primary fix is (a), a 1-file test-code correction. (b) is an environment/cleanup-tooling consideration that may warrant a separate follow-up if tenant_default.schema_migrations recurs on freshly-provisioned containers.
prevention: When writing or reviewing integration tests, always schema-qualify references to tables whose only legitimate copy lives in `public` (GBL-scoped, cross-tenant, or global bookkeeping tables) rather than relying on the ambient tenant_default,public search_path.
See docs/anti-patterns.md's existing entry for GitHub #338 / ISS-0089 for the same class of defect in a different file.
additional_evidence_rework1: Confirmed recurring during ISS-0107 rework-1 verification (WF03-iss0107-20260731, BACKEND-DEV, 2026-08-01). The `DROP TABLE tenant_default.schema_migrations` workaround was applied immediately before each of 2 full zig build test-integration runs, but the shadow table was observed recreated (empty, 0 rows) by the time each run completed -- i.e. some concurrently-running binary's tenant-schema provisioning path (bpm_provision_tenant_schema() and/or runMigrationsForSchema('tenant_default', ...), both invoked once per binary in TestHarness.init(), lines 447-451 of tests/integration/helpers.zig) recreates it every run, not just once historically on this long-lived container. This means the workaround only yields a clean measurement window at the very start of a run; db_integration_test.zig's own TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02 (bundled into the same test-integration-others-internal barrier as ~19+ siblings, with no dedicated single-binary build step to isolate them) can still race a sibling's re-provisioning and observe the shadow table again within the same run. Both runs' TC-DB-01-01 failed with 'expected 6, found 1' (unrelated 2nd defect also observed and separately worth noting: this specific assertion checks information_schema.tables in the public schema for 'events'/'instance_projections'/'instance_sequence'/'events_archive', which migration GBL-073_tnt01_drop_legacy_public_business_tables.sql intentionally moved out of public and into tenant_default long before this issue chain began -- so this particular assertion may need updating independent of the shadow-table fix once (a) is applied, since even correctly resolving to public.schema_migrations would not by itself fix an assertion checking for tables that were deliberately relocated). Both runs' TC-DB-01-02 failed with a growing count ('expected 293, found 330' run 1; 'expected 216, found 262' run 2), consistent with the unqualified reference resolving to the shared/growing shadow table mid-test. Candidate resolution (b) in this file (audit the provisioning path so the shadow table is not recreated) is elevated in priority by this evidence -- it is not a one-time historical artifact but an actively-recreated one on every run. This evidence gathered incidentally while verifying an unrelated fix (ISS-0107 lock_timeout scoping); ISS-0107's own acceptance criteria (zero deadlocks, zero 55P03 at the widened advisory-lock acquire) were independently confirmed met in both runs -- see docs/issues/ISS-0107.json.verification_result_rework1.
